summary: A 112-foot Cream City brick tower on Lake Michigan, lit in 1867 and encased in metal in 1900; its dwelling is now run for visitors, with the tower open to climb in season.

access.note: Reached only on foot or by bike from Ludington State Park; tower open to climb May to October for a fee.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Light-House Board reports (FY1899, FY1900) show the plan in FY1899, a contract on 14 December 1899 and completion in June 1900; the Michigan marker says 1902. Pepper gives $4,925; other web sources give other costs.

USLHS lists a fog signal building of 1897 and the Board's FY1899 report shows a steam whistle already running; Lighthouse Friends describes a brick fog signal building of 1908 first sounded 20 May 1909. Not reconciled.

notes_for_editor: NRHP nomination text is not digitised (22 KB placeholder), so the chronology rests on Lighthouse Friends and Terry Pepper (both modern, copyrighted; paraphrased with one short quotation each) plus Light-House Board reports. The Board reports in the local corpus cover only 1891-1901 and its Big Sable entries are headed 'Lake Superior' by mistake (the station is on Lake Michigan; the 1899 and 1900 reports use the name Grande Pointe au Sable). The 1868 to 1890 reports and the first-lighting date are not in the corpus, so 1 November 1867 rests on Lighthouse Friends alone. USLHS lists 'Fog Signal Building?: No' yet gives 1897 as year constructed. The fiscal year of the Commissioner passage (labelled 1921 by the corpus) was not checked against the page image; page numbers are scan pages. Spans in the roster (e.g. Alonzo Hyde vs Alonzo W. Hyde, Elsa J. Hyde) are as printed; relationships are not stated by any source read. The Lakeshore Keepers site and Lighthouse Friends' 'Sable Points Lighthouse Keepers Association' are probably the same body but no source read says so. Michigan State Historic Site status and the current characteristic/range in the record were not verified. The USCG historian page was blocked (403) and Wikipedia was used for leads only. Newspapers: one Chronicling America search found only a 1892 appropriations item. Roster position matches were taken from the USLHS printed lines (no OCR tables).
